source.title: On two long standing open problems on Lp-spaces

accepted.question_text: For each real p with 1 < p < infinity and p not equal to 2, does the Banach space Lp contain continuum many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces? Here Lp denotes the usual Lebesgue space, a complemented subspace means the range of a bounded projection on Lp, and two Banach spaces are considered the same only when they are linearly isomorphic.

evidence.quote: J. Bourgain, H.P. Rosenthal and G. Schechtman constructed uncountably many pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of Lp for 1 < p < infinity, p 6= 2 in [8] (it is unknown, whether there exists continuum such subspaces).

accepted.question_text: Is every complemented infinite-dimensional subspace of L1 isomorphic either to L1 itself or to the sequence space ell1? Here a complemented subspace of L1 is a closed subspace that is the range of a bounded projection on L1, and isomorphic means isomorphic as a Banach space.

evidence.quote: Problem 1 (Lindenstrauss and Rosenthal, 1969, [29]). Is every complemented infinite dimensional subspace of L1 isomorphic to either L1 or ell1?

accepted.question_text: Let E be an infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of L1. If E has the Schur property, meaning that weak convergence of a sequence in E always implies norm convergence, must E be isomorphic to ell1?

evidence.quote: Let E be an infinite dimensional complemented subspace of L1. Claim 1. If E has the Schur property then E is isomorphic to ell1.
As to the best of our knowledge, there is no information about Claim 1 in the literature.

accepted.question_text: Let P be a bounded projection on L1 whose range is a complemented subspace of L1 and suppose P is non-Dunford-Pettis, equivalently its range is not Schur in the formulation given by the source. Must P be an Enflo operator, meaning that P fixes a copy of L1; equivalently, is every non-Schur complemented subspace of L1 isomorphic to L1?

evidence.quote: An operator T in L(Lp,Y), 1 <= p < infinity, is called an Enflo operator provided T fixes a copy of Lp.
Problem 2 ([45], [14] and [7]). Must a non-Dunford-Pettis projection P in L(L1) be an Enflo operator? Equivalently, whether each non-Schur complemented subspace of L1 is isomorphic to L1?

accepted.question_text: For 1 <= p < infinity with p not equal to 2, is every regularly complemented subspace of Lp isomorphic either to ellp or to Lp? A subspace X of a Banach lattice E is regularly complemented when there exists a regular bounded projection from E onto X; a regular operator is one that can be written as the difference of two positive operators.

evidence.quote: An operator T : E -> F is called positive if T(E+) subset F+, and T : E -> F is called regular if T equals a difference of two positive operators.

We say that a subspace X of a Banach lattice is regularly complemented if there is a regular projection of E onto X. Problem 3. Let 1 <= p < infinity, p 6= 2. Is every regularly complemented subspace of Lp isomorphic to either ellp or Lp?

accepted.question_text: For a quasi-Banach Lebesgue space Lp with 0 < p < 1, is every complemented subspace of Lp isomorphic to Lp itself?

evidence.quote: Consider now the quasi-Banach spaces Lp for 0 < p < 1.
Problem 4. Let 0 <= p < 1. Is every complemented subspace of Lp isomorphic to Lp?

accepted.question_text: Let 1 <= p < infinity with p not equal to 2, and let (Omega, Sigma, mu) be a finite atomless measure space such that the density character dim Lp(mu) is strictly larger than aleph_0 and strictly smaller than aleph_{omega_0}. Does Lp(mu) have an unconditional basis, in the nonseparable sense that every element has a unique at most countable unconditional expansion over the basis family?

evidence.quote: A (not ordered) family (xi)i in I of elements of a (non-separable) Banach space X is called an unconditional basis of X if every x in X admits a unique representation x = sum_i in I ai xi, where the set of all indices i in I with ai 6= 0 is at most countable, and the series converges unconditionally.

Problem 5 (P. Enflo and H.P. Rosenthal, 1973, [13]). Let 1 <= p < infinity, p 6= 2, and let (Omega, Sigma, mu) be a finite atomless measure space with aleph_0 < dim Lp(mu) < aleph_omega0. Is there an unconditional basis of Lp(mu)?

accepted.question_text: For 1 <= p < infinity with p not equal to 2, does the nonseparable Lebesgue space Lp({-1,1}^{omega_1}) have an unconditional basis? The measure on {-1,1}^{omega_1} is the product probability measure with each coordinate assigning mass 1/2 to -1 and 1/2 to 1.
accepted.context_brief: Unconditional bases in Lp of the first uncountable product cube

evidence.quote: mu_omega_alpha is the Haar measure on the compact Abelian group {-1, 1}^omega_alpha with the point-wise product.
Problem 6. Let 1 <= p < infinity, p 6= 2. Does there exist an unconditional basis in Lp{-1, 1}^omega1?

accepted.question_text: Let 1 <= p < infinity with p not equal to 2. Let Ep be Lp([0,1]^2) with Lebesgue measure on the square, and let Fp be the closed subspace of Ep consisting of functions that depend only on the first coordinate. Does Ep have an unconditional basis that can be split as (fn) union (gn), with the closed linear span of the fn equal to Fp, such that the unconditional constant of the subsequence (fn) is exactly the same as the unconditional constant of the full basis (fn) union (gn)?

evidence.quote: The number M is called the unconditional constant of the unconditional basis (xn).

Let Ep = Lp[0, 1]^2 be the Lp-space over the Lebesgue measure space of Borel subsets of the square [0, 1]^2, and let Fp be the subspace of Ep consisting of all functions depending only on the first variable.

Problem 7. Let 1 <= p < infinity, p 6= 2. Does there exist an unconditional basis (fn) union (gn) in Ep consisting of two parts such that [fn] = Fp and the unconditional constant of (fn) equals the unconditional constant of the entire basis (fn) union (gn)?

accepted.question_text: Does a positive answer to the separable model problem for Ep = Lp([0,1]^2), namely the existence of an unconditional basis (fn) union (gn) whose fn part spans the first-coordinate subspace Fp and has the same unconditional constant as the full basis, formally imply a positive answer to the nonseparable problem asking whether Lp({-1,1}^{omega_1}) has an unconditional basis for 1 <= p < infinity and p not equal to 2?
accepted.context_brief: Implication between the separable and nonseparable basis problems

evidence.quote: We do not know of whether an affirmative solution to Problem 7 formally implies an affirmative solution to Problem 6.

trace.notes: Normalized the single input as the zbMATH bibliographic resolver URL https://zbmath.org/7252022 with trailing identifier 7252022.

Local workflow resolver rows in outputs/shards/open-problems-shard-0.csv and outputs/open-problems-0418-all.csv identify the exact zbMATH record title as 'On two long standing open problems on L_p-spaces', year 2020, and DOI link https://doi.org/10.15330/cmp.12.1.229-241.

Exact-title and DOI search recovered the Carpathian Mathematical Publications article page and direct PDF. Local shell download failed with network_or_dns_failure for journals.pnu.edu.ua, so extraction used the readable PDF text exposed by the web reader at the publisher download URL. The PDF title and DOI match the resolver metadata.

Mapped the 13-page PDF: title and abstract on page 1; Section 1 introduction; Section 2 on complemented subspaces of Lp with subsections 2.1-2.6 and problem regions in 2.3-2.6; Section 3 on unconditional bases in Lp(mu) with subsections 3.1-3.5 and problem regions in 3.3-3.5.
Section 2.3 contains one implicit unknown question about continuum many complemented subspaces of Lp and the explicit Lindenstrauss-Rosenthal Problem 1 for complemented subspaces of L1.
Section 2.4 contains Claim 1 as an explicit unresolved subproblem and Problem 2 about non-Dunford-Pettis projections or non-Schur complemented subspaces of L1.
Section 2.5 contains Problem 3 about regularly complemented subspaces of Lp.
Section 2.6 contains Problem 4 about complemented subspaces of quasi-Banach Lp spaces for 0 < p < 1.
Section 3.3 contains Problem 5, the Enflo-Rosenthal question about unconditional bases in nonseparable Lp(mu) below density aleph_omega0.
Section 3.4 contains a partial question about the first four functions of the Olevskii system being isometrically reproducible in any unconditional basis of Lp{-1,1}^omega1.
Section 3.5 contains Problem 6 on unconditional bases in Lp{-1,1}^omega1, Problem 7 on a separable two-part basis in Ep, and a later remark asking whether Problem 7 formally implies Problem 6.
Expanded 'continuum such subspaces' to pairwise non-isomorphic complemented subspaces of Lp for 1 < p < infinity, p not equal to 2, using the immediately preceding sentence.
Rewrote Problem 1 as a standalone dichotomy for infinite-dimensional complemented subspaces of L1.
Expanded Claim 1 with the source's definition of the Schur property from page 3 and the ambient assumption that E is an infinite-dimensional complemented subspace of L1.
Expanded Problem 2 using the source definition of Enflo operator and included the equivalent non-Schur complemented-subspace formulation from the problem statement.
Expanded Problem 3 with the source definitions of regular operator and regularly complemented subspace.
Used the section heading context 0 < p < 1 to avoid treating the printed 0 <= p < 1 in Problem 4 as introducing an unsupported L0 case.
Expanded Problem 5 with the source's nonseparable unconditional-basis convention and density-character notation.
Expanded Problem 6 with the product-measure meaning of {-1,1}^omega1 from the Maharam-model discussion.
Expanded Problem 7 with definitions of Ep, Fp, closed linear span [fn], and unconditional constant from the surrounding text.
Expanded the remark about whether Problem 7 implies Problem 6 by restating both problems rather than referring back to their labels.

Kept the Olevskii-system partial question in needs_review because the source does not define 'isometrically reproducible' precisely enough in the available evidence to make a fully self-contained accepted rewrite without adding unsupported detail.

No candidates were merged. Problem 1, Claim 1, and Problem 2 are related but ask different dichotomy, Schur, and non-Schur projection questions; Problems 5, 6, 7, and the implication remark are nested but distinct.
Accepted q_001 through q_010: each has a standalone rewritten question, at least one page-numbered evidence quote, no solved label, and no unsupported solved-status claim.

Moved to needs_review because the required source-specific term 'isometrically reproducible' is not defined with enough precision in the source evidence to pass the self-containedness and no-new-facts gates.
